items.title: Art Farmer — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: working with Teddy was very beneficial to me... We worked most of the time with a quartet.

ctx.x: It kind of presages, yet very ironic that you end living in the country where German is spoken. I want to backtrack just a little bit because we talked about your work in the avant-garde, and there was a group that you were working with earlier on called New Directions.

Teddy Charles, yeah. Damn, that’s when I first got here and working with Teddy was very beneficial to me because that’s where my reputation started of being a person that was sympathetic to whatever everyone wrote, and I was willing to do my damnedest to play it the way they wrote it. I would take it home and study it and practice it. That’s where it all started, through Teddy, New Directions. We worked most of the time with a quartet. Mingus was in the group sometimes. I remember one time we were playing in…
Who else was in that group? Who was on drums…
